candidates.title: PMP CSRs (pmpcfg0-15, pmpaddr0-63) raise illegal-instruction in M-mode instead of reading as WARL read-only zero, an undocumented deviation in the privilege/memory-permission CSR file
candidates.component: Interpreter CSR file (main processor), shared by native, uarch, log producers and all verifiers
candidates.role: Honest operator (interpreter, per the AUDIT.md component table); the same code is the state transition function the uarch and the on-chain step implement
candidates.location: src/interpret.cpp read_csr (~2005-2163, default case -> read_csr_fail) and write_csr (~2489-2640, default case -> failure); src/riscv-constants.hpp enum CSR_address (no 0x3A0-0x3EF entries)
candidates.description: The CSR file has no entries for the PMP CSRs pmpcfg0..pmpcfg15 (0x3A0-0x3AF) and pmpaddr0..pmpaddr63 (0x3B0-0x3EF). Any CSR instruction on them, even in M-mode, falls into the default case of read_csr/write_csr and raises an illegal-instruction exception (mcause 2, mtval = instruction). The privileged specification (3.7.1, 20211203) says implementations may implement zero, 16 or 64 PMP entries, that 'All PMP CSR fields are WARL and may be read-only zero' and that 'PMP CSRs are only accessible to M-mode': with zero entries the CSRs still exist and read as zero, writes are ignored (the Spike reference model creates all 64 pmpaddr/pmpcfg CSRs and ignores writes beyond n_pmp). The manual (doc/README.md 'The main processor') lists the ISA and Sv39 and never mentions PMP or this deviation. The behavior is deterministic and identical on all paths (same interpret.cpp), so it is not a divergence; it is an undocumented architectural deviation in the 'Privilege levels' / 'memory permissions' area of R7. Earlier round notes mention it as 'not reported' (R1 R7 note); it was never a candidate. It is the PMP-site analogue of R1-R7-3 (hpmcounter), but PMP CSRs belong to the base privileged architecture rather than to the optional Zihpm extension.
candidates.trigger: Any guest code (after an input takes control, or the template's own M-mode firmware) executing csrr/csrw on pmpcfgN/pmpaddrN in M-mode. No configuration change needed.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from every valid template: one M-mode CSR instruction. Verified: in a fresh machine at mcycle 0 in M-mode, 'csrr a0, pmpcfg0' traps with mcause=2, mtval=0x3a002573.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no exclusion applies (no API misuse, no unreproducible machine, not guest-software defect; the deviation is the emulator's). 2 Role: interpreter = honest operator; the behavior is also what the uarch program and on-chain verifier implement, so it is part of the state transition function. 3 High/Medium cases: matches Medium 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7).' A spec-conformant firmware cannot rely on PMP writes for isolation on a zero-entry hart (writes are ignored there; it must read back), so trapping instead does not weaken isolation; OpenSBI probes PMP with a trap-safe read. 4 Critical (alternative reading): R7 'any deviation lets an input subvert a correct guest, even a deviation that is consistent across all paths' in 'Privilege levels' and 'Address translation and memory permissions' would make it Critical if PMP CSR existence is read as part of those areas; decided by whether a correct guest may execute an unguarded PMP CSR access in M-mode on a hart whose documentation does not say PMP is absent. 5 Low (alternative reading): if trapping on unimplemented PMP CSRs is read as allowed by the specification (as some implementations treat PMP as absent), it is at most a manual omission.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (preferred) / Critical (literal R7) / Low (if absent PMP CSRs may trap)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Does not let a claim settle a wrong state (all paths agree). It violates R7 ('The emulator implements the RISC-V specification ... departing only where the manual documents a deviation'): a guest written to the privileged specification that writes pmpcfg0 (for example to lock down or clear PMP at boot) without a trap handler takes an unexpected illegal-instruction trap, which an adversarial input can not exploit for state divergence but which changes guest-visible semantics in the privilege area.
candidates.evidence: Scratch test SUBCSR/pmp.lua: machine with RAM at 0x80000000 holding 'csrr a0,pmpcfg0; csrr a1,pmpaddr0; j .' and mtvec=0x80000008; after run(1): pc=0x80000008, mcause=0x2, mtval=0x3a002573. Code reading: CSR_address has no PMP addresses; read_csr/write_csr default -> fail.
candidates.test_idea: Lua test: build a 3-instruction RAM image ('csrr a0,pmpcfg0; csrw pmpaddr0,a0; ...'), set mtvec to a halting stub, run a few mcycles in M-mode, and assert mcause != 2 (no illegal-instruction trap), x10 == 0 after the read, and that a subsequent read of pmpaddr0 after a write returns 0 (WARL read-only zero). Fails today (mcause=2), passes once PMP CSRs are hardwired to zero or the manual documents the deviation (in which case the test should check the manual text instead).

candidates.title: WARL legalization from configuration is incomplete: read-only mstatus fields (VS, UBE, SBE, MBE, UXL, SXL, SD vs VS) and misa are accepted verbatim and become guest-visible
candidates.component: Machine creation (machine::init_processor raw write_reg) and the WARL-on-read legalizers (src/riscv-warl.hpp WARL_mstatus; misa has none)
candidates.role: Honest operator (machine creation and interpreter per AUDIT.md); support-level impact only since triggering needs a non-default configuration
candidates.location: src/riscv-warl.hpp WARL_mstatus (masks with MSTATUS_R_MASK only, recomputes SD from FS only); src/riscv-constants.hpp MSTATUS_R_MASK (includes VS, UBE, SBE, MBE, UXL, SXL); src/i-state-access.hpp DEFINE_SA_READ(misa) (no WARL); src/machine.cpp init_processor (~130-198) and write_reg (~1366, 1384) store raw values without validation
candidates.description: riscv-warl.hpp states that the WARL functions 'ensure WARL registers always hold legal values, even if written with arbitrary data through external APIs', and every interpreter read of mstatus goes through WARL_mstatus. But WARL_mstatus only clears bits outside MSTATUS_R_MASK, legalizes MPP=HS and forces FS Dirty/SD. Fields that are read-only for this hart keep whatever the configuration wrote: VS (no V extension: must be read-only 0), UBE/SBE/MBE (little-endian only: must be 0), UXL/SXL (RV64 only: must be 2). SD is recomputed from FS alone, so a configuration with VS=Dirty and FS=Off reads SD=0, an inconsistent combination. misa is not legalized at all (raw read), so a configuration can advertise extensions the interpreter does not implement (H, V, ...) or hide ones it does. Machine creation accepts all of these without error.
candidates.trigger: The party that writes the template's machine configuration (trusted) sets processor.registers.mstatus or misa to such a value; the guest then reads mstatus/sstatus/misa.
candidates.reachability: Only through a configuration holding values the RISC-V specification does not allow for this hart; not reachable by guest instructions from a valid template (the write masks exclude these fields and misa writes are ignored). Verified: config mstatus=0x3a00000640 (VS=3, UBE=SBE=MBE=1) reads back 0x3a00000640 (SD=0); mstatus=0x500000000 (UXL=SXL=1) reads back verbatim; misa with bit 7 (H) set reads back with H; native and uarch agree in every case.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: arguably 'the effect of a deliberate state change made through the machine API' for configuration values, but creation from a configuration is the documented way to build templates, so not clearly excluded. 2 Role: machine creation and interpreter (honest operator). 3 High/Medium cases: none; all paths agree (no divergence). R4's configuration clause covers only configurations 'holding only register values that the RISC-V specification and the manual allow', and these values are not allowed for this hart, so a template holding them is not a valid template ('Its registers hold only values that the RISC-V specification and the manual allow for them'). 4 Critical: no rule is violated at a reachable state, since no input sequence from a valid template produces these fields (write masks MSTATUS_W_MASK/SSTATUS_W_MASK exclude them, misa writes are ignored, traps and xRET only touch MIE/SIE/MPIE/SPIE/MPP/SPP/MPRV). 5 Low: a real defect (the code's own invariant and the angle's invariant 'no CSR ever holds a value the specification disallows' fail for configuration-loaded values; a configuration that 'would not' be valid is not rejected).
candidates.threat_to_goal: None directly: every path legalizes identically. It only weakens the defense-in-depth that WARL-on-read is meant to provide and lets a mis-written template advertise a big-endian or 32-bit U/S mode or a V/H extension to its guest, which the emulator does not implement.
candidates.evidence: Scratch test SUBCSR/warl.lua: creates machines with the listed mstatus/misa values, runs 'csrr a0,mstatus; csrr a1,misa; csrr a2,sstatus', prints the guest-visible values, and checks that run_uarch+reset_uarch per mcycle reaches the same root hash (it does).
candidates.test_idea: Lua test: for each of mstatus VS=3, MBE=1, UXL=1 and misa with bit 'H' set, either expect cartesi.machine(config) to raise an error, or run 'csrr a0,mstatus' / 'csrr a1,misa' and assert VS==0, UBE==SBE==MBE==0, UXL==SXL==2, SD consistent with FS/VS, misa == the implemented ISA. Fails today.

not_covered: No randomized native-vs-uarch differential of trap-heavy S/U-mode guests with medeleg delegation and Sv39 paging; delegation, exception priority and mtval values were checked by reading raise_exception, fetch_insn, read/write_virtual_memory_slow, execute_SC/AMO only (all paths share interpret.cpp, so divergence could only come from state-access differences, not re-examined here).

Interrupt-check invariant (native checks only at RTC ticks and after success_and_serve_interrupts; uarch checks every mcycle): established by enumerating every writer of iprv/mstatus.MIE,SIE/mie/mip/mideleg (CSR writes, xRET, raise_exception, CLINT msip/mtimecmp, PLIC claim/complete, update_rtc_interrupt) and their return statuses; no dynamic search for a counterexample.
PLIC/SEIP conflation and PLIC behavior with configuration-set girqpend/girqsrvd (not reachable in reproducible machines from the default configuration); not tested.
Unreproducible-only paths: WFI polling (poll_external_interrupts), soft yield, VirtIO interrupts.
Soft-float, fflags accrual and rounding-mode semantics beyond the FS/frm legality checks.
Address translation details (superpages, Sv48 walks, A/D updates, MPRV with config-only prv/MPP combinations) beyond the TLB flush conditions on mstatus/satp/privilege changes.
Configuration-only spec-illegal values of non-WARL registers (iprv=2 or >3, odd pc, iflags combinations, raw mcause) beyond reading their consumers.
The manual's reference to privileged spec v1.10 (doc/README.md ~4524) versus implemented 1.12 features (menvcfg/senvcfg, MPRV clearing on xRET) was noticed but not analysed.
